name: Rear Brake Pads
summary: Rear pad job on the E90 uses a floating caliper with a separate mechanical drum-in-hat parking brake, so no electronic parking brake retraction is needed. Rear pad PN 34216774692 and rear sensor 34356789445 are verified by two retailers each, with a build-date split (03/2010 onward has other numbers). Caliper bolt torque is not verified and a conflict exists on tool size and which side carries the rear sensor.
variantDependencies: Engine (N52B30 vs N51B30 SULEV) UNCONFIRMED: no evidence found that the brake/tire/wiper jobs differ by engine; not a tracked dependency but unverified.
RWD vs xDrive UNCONFIRMED: front wear sensor part number differs (34356789441 listed for xi/xDrive vs 34356789440 for non-xi); front jack point differs on xDrive.
Production date UNCONFIRMED: retailer fitment splits at 03/2010 (wear sensors) and 09/2009 (wipers); a 2010 model year car may fall on either side.
Brake package UNCONFIRMED: retailers split fitment between 'standard' and 'M Performance' front brakes (larger front brake); front pad part number depends on it.
Transmission (manual vs auto) UNCONFIRMED: no evidence it affects these jobs.
Rear sensor: 34356789445 (through about 03/2010 build) vs 34356792564 (listed for builds from 03/2010; 328i not named).
Rear pad PN: 34216774692 listed to 2009 (Turner) vs 2010 (PMB); 34216790761 (Jurid) lists 2009-2012 328i xDrive; Team-BHP lists 34216791938 and 34216769105. Brake package/rotor size may matter.
xDrive: fitment tables list 328i xDrive rear pads from 2009; xDrive-specific differences in rear brake hardware not established.

Parking brake: mechanical cable drum-in-hat on E90 per two retailer/forum sources (Turner shoe set and adjusting screw for E90 325i/328i sedan; bimmerpost thread); no electronic parking brake on this chassis. Not verified against a BMW document.

tools.item: Jack and stands; rear jack point is the black cast-iron differential housing, not the aluminum cover (forum)
Guide-bolt tool: 17 mm hex socket (Team-BHP) vs 5/8 in socket (bmwtuning) -- conflict
Piston retraction: spreader or C-clamp (plain push-back; no rotate/wind-back tool required per the sources found)
Flat-blade screwdriver (anti-rattle clip, plastic caps, sensor clip)
10 mm socket for wheel-liner bolts to reach sensor
Brake cleaner, guide-pin grease, anti-squeal paste
No EPB service-mode tool needed (mechanical handbrake)

parts.item: Rear pad set, genuine/OEM-equivalent (Pagid listing: 328i/328xi/328i xDrive sedan 2006-2009; PMB: 328i 2007-2010, 328i xDrive 2009-2010)
Rear pad set named in Team-BHP list (alt)
Rear pad set named in Team-BHP list (alt)
Rear pad wear sensor for builds from 03/2010 (328i not named; unverified)
Parking-brake shoe set (only if inspecting/replacing; not part of pad job)

torque.conflicts: Secondary sources only; no BMW document.
One M3 poster gives 22 ft-lb front and rear; single source, M3 context.

torque.fastener: Rear caliper carrier bolts (only if removed)

steps.title: Loosen wheel bolts, lift, support
steps.instruction: Loosen wheel bolts on the ground, lift using the rear differential housing point and place stands at the jacking points, remove wheels.
warnings: Do not lift on the aluminum diff cover.

steps.title: Optional: open reservoir cap
steps.instruction: Opening the reservoir lid under the hood eases piston retraction; watch the level.

steps.title: Remove anti-rattle clip
steps.instruction: Pry the clip out by working between the hub and the caliper.

steps.title: Unclip rear sensor (one side only)
steps.instruction: One source says only the left rear has a sensor; another says passenger side. Check both wheel wells and free the cable from the pad.
warnings: Left vs passenger-side conflict; US left = driver side.

steps.title: Remove guide bolts and caliper
steps.instruction: Pop the caps, loosen then remove the two guide bolts (top and bottom), lift the caliper off the rotor and support it.
warnings: Hex/socket size conflict (17 mm vs 5/8 in).
Do not hang caliper from hose.

steps.title: Remove pads
steps.instruction: Pull the outer pad, then pry the inner pad from the piston clips.

steps.title: Retract piston
steps.instruction: Push the piston back with a spreader/clamp using the old pad as backing. No parking-brake mechanism is inside the caliper; the handbrake shoes sit inside the rotor hat.

steps.title: Clean and lube
steps.instruction: Clean the carrier and sliding surfaces, grease guide pins, apply paste only to metal contact points.
warnings: Keep brake cleaner off rubber and paint.

steps.title: Fit sensor and new pads
steps.instruction: Remove wheel-liner bolts if needed to reach the sensor mounting; fit the correct-length rear sensor and route the cable as before.
warnings: A wrong-length sensor was fitted first by the Team-BHP author; check length.

steps.title: Reassemble and torque
steps.instruction: Refit caliper and guide bolts to specification (value MISSING), caps on, then wheels torqued to 120 Nm.

steps.title: Seat pads and test
steps.instruction: Pump the pedal until firm and test at low speed.

steps.title: Reset rear brake service
steps.instruction: Use cluster reset (rear brake symbol) with a new rear sensor, or a BMW-capable scan tool via Service > Maintenance > CBS reset, rear brake.
warnings: Reset needs a new sensor fitted.

safety: Parking brake is mechanical drum-in-hat (no EPB retract procedure needed); do not rely on it as sole restraint on stands.
Do not let the caliper hang from the brake hose.
Do not contaminate friction surfaces with grease.
